title: Tech 08 Observability Sampling
decision: Choose telemetry sampling policy under cost and incident-detection constraints.
context: A platform collects traces from hundreds of services.
Trace volume has doubled and the telemetry bill exceeds budget.
Rare errors are disproportionately valuable for diagnosis.
constraints: Telemetry cost must fall by at least 40 percent.
All error traces and very slow requests should remain available.
Normal-request sampling must still support service-level latency analysis.
options: Uniformly sample every trace at 10 percent.
Use head-based 1 percent sampling for all requests.
Use tail-aware sampling that retains errors and slow traces plus a lower random sample of normal traffic.

evidence.fact: Only 0.7 percent of requests return errors, but error traces account for 46 percent of traces used during incident reviews.
Requests above the p99 latency threshold represent 1 percent of volume.
Normal successful traffic represents more than 98 percent of trace volume.
A prototype tail sampler reduced stored trace volume by 55 percent while retaining all injected error and p99 test traces.
Metrics are collected independently at full aggregation and do not depend on retaining every trace.
The telemetry backend can apply different retention rules after spans are assembled, enabling tail-based decisions before storage.
